title: Does Content Moderation Lead Users Away from Fringe Movements? Evidence from a Recovery Community

live_model.evidence: "we used GPT-4-turbo, a large language model, to further evaluate the nature of comments...GPT-4-turbo labeled 97% of the comments as compliant with the community guidelines, and 99% did not align with the values of the fringe communities."

prompt.location: "We provide the prompts used in the Appendix."
prompt.note: Two prompting strategies: (1) community guidelines + comment, ask if it violates rules; (2) fringe-community ideology descriptions + comment, ask if aligned.

claim.metric: none validated against ground truth (97%/99% are raw label distributions on real Reddit comments, not an accuracy score)
claim.location: LLM Moderation Analysis section; item count (all newcomer/migrant comments in the 120-day observation window) not stated as a single number in the retrieved text

data.source: Reddit comments from r/exredpill and related fringe subreddits (r/Braincels, r/MGTOW, r/TheRedPill); not a released dataset

notes: GPT-4-turbo is used purely as a content annotator (role A) for a social-science claim about community recovery; its 97%/99% figures are the classifier's raw output distribution on real user comments, not a capability score checked against independent ground truth (contrast with a validated annotator like W4399911093), and the exact item count is not given as a single reproducible n.
